plotBoard.emptySub: Start from a proven plot structure, or build your own from scratch.
plotBoard.intro: The {plotBoard} is a two-axis grid: narrative strands across the rows, chapters across the columns. Each beat sits at its strand × chapter intersection. Drag beats around, click an empty cell to add one, and {applyTemplate} lays a standard structural framework (Three-Act, Save the Cat, Hero's Journey, Story Circle) over your outline.
plotBoard.removeBeatTooltip: Remove this beat from the strand

dialog.deleteBody: Delete "{name}" and all its beats? You can restore it from Trash.

plotBoard.deleteStrandTooltip: Delete this strand and all its beats

threeAct.label: Three-Act Structure
threeAct.blurb: The classic backbone: setup, confrontation, resolution. Six beats marking the major turning points.

hook.label: Hook
hook.note: Open with something that demands attention.

incitingIncident.label: Inciting incident
incitingIncident.note: The event that disrupts ordinary life and starts the story.

firstPlotPoint.label: First plot point
firstPlotPoint.note: End of Act I — the protagonist commits to the journey.

midpoint.label: Midpoint
midpoint.note: A revelation or shift that recenters the stakes.

climax.label: Climax
climax.note: Final confrontation — the question of the story gets answered.

fiveAct.label: Five-Act Structure
fiveAct.blurb: Freytag's pyramid: exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, dénouement. Useful for tragedies and ensemble dramas.

exposition.label: Exposition
exposition.note: Establish the world, characters, and status quo.

incitingMoment.label: Inciting moment
incitingMoment.note: The first disturbance that pulls characters toward conflict.

risingAction.label: Rising action
risingAction.note: Stakes escalate; alliances and obstacles emerge.

turn.label: Turn
turn.note: A crucial decision or revelation that changes trajectory.

denouement.label: Dénouement
denouement.note: Tie up loose threads. Show the new equilibrium (or its absence).

saveTheCat.label: Save the Cat
saveTheCat.blurb: Blake Snyder's 15-beat sheet. Tight scaffolding popular for genre fiction and screenplays.

openingImage.label: Opening Image
openingImage.note: A single image that captures the protagonist's status quo.

themeStated.label: Theme Stated
themeStated.note: Someone (not the hero) states the moral question of the story.

setUp.label: Set-Up
setUp.note: Hero's flaw is shown. Stakes hinted at. Around 10% of the book.

debate.label: Debate
debate.note: Hero hesitates. Asks the central question.

breakIntoTwo.label: Break Into Two
breakIntoTwo.note: Hero commits and crosses into the new world (~25%).

bStory.label: B Story
bStory.note: Subplot begins — usually love or mentor. Carries the theme.

funAndGames.label: Fun and Games
funAndGames.note: The promise of the premise. Spectacle, set pieces, joy.

midpoint.label: Midpoint
midpoint.note: False victory or false defeat. Stakes raised (~50%).

allIsLost.label: All Is Lost
allIsLost.note: Whiff of death. The opposite of the opening image (~75%).

breakIntoThree.label: Break Into Three
breakIntoThree.note: A and B stories converge. Hero finds the answer.

finale.label: Finale
finale.note: Hero storms the castle. Old world dismantled, new world built.

finalImage.label: Final Image
finalImage.note: Mirror of the opening image — shows transformation.

herosJourney.label: Hero's Journey
herosJourney.blurb: Campbell's monomyth via Vogler. Twelve stages mapping the archetypal transformation arc.

ordinaryWorld.label: Ordinary World
ordinaryWorld.note: Hero in their familiar environment, before the call.

callToAdventure.label: Call to Adventure
callToAdventure.note: A challenge, problem, or opportunity appears.

meetingTheMentor.label: Meeting the Mentor
meetingTheMentor.note: Guidance, gift, or wisdom from a wiser figure.

crossingTheThreshold.label: Crossing the Threshold
crossingTheThreshold.note: Hero commits and enters the special world.

testsAlliesEnemies.label: Tests, Allies, Enemies
testsAlliesEnemies.note: First trials. Hero learns the rules of the new world.

ordeal.label: Ordeal
ordeal.note: The crisis at the heart of the journey. Symbolic death.

reward.label: Reward
reward.note: Hero seizes the prize and survives the ordeal.

theRoadBack.label: The Road Back
theRoadBack.note: Hero leaves the special world. Pursuit begins.

resurrection.label: Resurrection
resurrection.note: A final test that completes the transformation.

returnWithTheElixir.label: Return with the Elixir
returnWithTheElixir.note: Hero returns home changed, bringing something that heals the ordinary world.

storyCircle.label: Story Circle
storyCircle.blurb: Dan Harmon's eight-step distillation of the monomyth. Compact and recursive — works at chapter or arc level.

you.label: You
you.note: A character in a zone of comfort.

take.label: Take
take.note: Pay a heavy price for it.

return.label: Return
return.note: Then return to their familiar situation.

brainstorm.title: Brainstorm
brainstorm.intro: {brainstorm} is a transient generator for names and short phrases — character names, place names, object/item names, titles, or any free-form list. Pick a category, type a seed, hit Generate; thumbs-up the ones you like and click {moreLikeThese} to steer the next batch. Nothing here persists once you leave the panel — copy what you want and move on.
brainstorm.seedHint: Describe vibe, genre, era, register, sound — the more specific the seed, the less generic the output.
brainstorm.generateTooltip: Generate ideas from your seed prompt
brainstorm.generateDisabledTooltip: Enter a seed prompt to generate ideas
brainstorm.moreLikeTooltip: Generate more results similar to your liked items
brainstorm.moreLikeDisabledTooltip: Thumb-up at least one result to steer the next batch
brainstorm.thumbHint: Thumb-up results to steer the next batch.
brainstorm.emptyHint: Pick a category, describe what you need, and hit Generate.

character_name.label: Character names
character_name.purpose: Personal names for a character — given names, surnames, full names, nicknames.
character_name.placeholder:
e.g. Norse-sounding female warrior names, sharp consonants, two syllables.

Or: Reedy academic name for a 1920s English don, slightly ridiculous.

place_name.label: Place names
place_name.purpose: Toponyms — cities, taverns, neighbourhoods, mountains, ships, kingdoms, planets.
place_name.placeholder:
e.g. Creepy New England small-town shop names, 1920s setting.

Or: Frontier-town tavern names that suggest both refuge and trouble.

item_name.label: Item / object names
item_name.purpose: Names for things — swords, books, organisations, spells, drugs, vehicles, recurring objects.
item_name.placeholder:
e.g. Names for a legendary sword passed down by exiled queens, evocative not ornate.

Or: Old-fashioned names for a banned political pamphlet circulated in the 1840s.

title.label: Titles (book / chapter / scene)
title.purpose: Book titles, chapter titles, or scene titles — short, evocative, register-aware.
title.placeholder:
e.g. Titles for a heist novel set on a generation ship, single word, evocative.

Or: Chapter titles for a slow-burn romance — three-to-five words, melancholy.

next_beat.label: Next plot beats
next_beat.purpose: Brainstorm what could happen next at the plot level — moves, beats, escalations from where the story currently sits. Different from "Continue" in the editor: this gives you a menu of options, not finished prose.
next_beat.placeholder:
e.g. Elena has just confirmed Marcus is lying. She has the locket but no allies left. Generate 15–20 possible next plot beats — escalations, complications, reveals, twists, scene moves.

Or: The crew has reached the temple. Tomas wants to enter; Esme wants to wait. Brainstorm where the scene goes next.

twist.label: Plot twists
twist.purpose: Twists, reveals, and unexpected turns the story could take — from plausible to wild. Excellent for when the next move feels too obvious, or for a brainstorm even when you reject most options.
twist.placeholder:
e.g. Mid-second-act thriller. Detective protagonist is closing in on the killer. Brainstorm 15–20 plot twists — revelations, reversals, identity shifts, betrayals — from plausible to wild.

Or: Quiet literary novel about a daughter caring for an aging father. What could twist the dynamic?

free.label: Anything (free prompt)
free.purpose: Use this when the category list doesn't fit — phrases, taglines, alternate words, ideas.
free.placeholder:
e.g. Twenty short phrases a tired innkeeper might say to a stranger before bed.

Or: Twenty single words that mean both 'home' and 'cage'.

worldbuilding.emptyBody: Long-form articles for lore, magic systems, cultures — anything you'd put in an appendix. AI features pull relevant articles as story-world context.
worldbuilding.intro: A {articleTerm} is long-form reference that doesn't belong on a character, location, or object sheet — a magic system, a kingdom's history, an invented language, a calendar, a religion. Organise articles by category, tag them freely; AI features that draw on story-world context will reach for the article when it's relevant.

beatSheet.title: Map to a narrative framework
beatSheet.blurb: Pick a framework. JustWrite maps each of its beats to the chapter that best fulfils it — and flags the beats your book doesn't cover. The model's instructed to be honest about {missing} beats; a clean map of every beat is suspicious. Best after a complete draft.

err.noProvider: Configure an AI provider in Settings → AI to map to a beat sheet.

saveTheCat.name: Save the Cat
saveTheCat.blurb: Blake Snyder's 15-beat sheet. Built for commercial film, widely used in genre novels.

openingImage.name: Opening Image
openingImage.desc: A snapshot of the protagonist's status quo. The thing the story will change.

themeStated.name: Theme Stated
themeStated.desc: Someone, usually not the protagonist, states the story's thematic premise — often without realising its weight.

setup.name: Setup
setup.desc: The protagonist's world, their want, their flaw, and the people who pull on them.

catalyst.name: Catalyst
catalyst.desc: The inciting event that disrupts the status quo.

debate.name: Debate
debate.desc: The protagonist resists or hesitates. Should they engage with the catalyst?

breakIntoTwo.name: Break Into Two
breakIntoTwo.desc: The protagonist commits. The world of Act II begins.

bStory.name: B Story
bStory.desc: A second storyline (often relational or thematic) opens, usually with a new character.

funAndGames.name: Fun and Games
funAndGames.desc: The promise of the premise — the scenes the reader came for.

midpoint.name: Midpoint
midpoint.desc: A false victory or false defeat that raises the stakes.

badGuysCloseIn.name: Bad Guys Close In
badGuysCloseIn.desc: External pressure mounts; the protagonist's flaws start to undermine them.

allIsLost.name: All Is Lost
allIsLost.desc: The lowest point. Often involves a death (literal or figurative).

darkNightOfSoul.name: Dark Night of the Soul
darkNightOfSoul.desc: The protagonist faces themselves. The internal turn that enables the external turn.

breakIntoThree.name: Break Into Three
breakIntoThree.desc: A new understanding (often catalysed by the B Story) enables a new plan.

finale.name: Finale
finale.desc: The protagonist executes the plan. The story's external and internal arcs converge.

finalImage.name: Final Image
finalImage.desc: A mirror of the Opening Image showing how the world has changed.

herosJourney.name: Hero's Journey
herosJourney.blurb: Christopher Vogler's 12-stage adaptation of Joseph Campbell's monomyth. Strong for fantasy, sci-fi, and mythic structure.

callToAdventure.name: Call to Adventure
callToAdventure.desc: An invitation, a problem, or a wound that pulls them toward change.

refusalOfCall.name: Refusal of the Call
refusalOfCall.desc: The hero hesitates, doubts, or refuses outright.

meetingMentor.name: Meeting the Mentor
meetingMentor.desc: Wisdom, training, or a gift that enables the journey.

crossingThreshold.name: Crossing the Threshold
crossingThreshold.desc: The hero leaves the ordinary world and enters a new one.

testsAlliesEnemies.name: Tests, Allies, Enemies
testsAlliesEnemies.desc: The hero learns the new world's rules and gathers a cast.

approachInmostCave.name: Approach to the Inmost Cave
approachInmostCave.desc: Preparation for the central ordeal. Plans, fears, last conversations.

ordeal.name: Ordeal
ordeal.desc: The central life-or-death confrontation. The hero touches death and finds something.

reward.name: Reward (Seizing the Sword)
reward.desc: The hero claims what the ordeal made possible.

roadBack.name: The Road Back
roadBack.desc: The hero starts the return. New dangers and the pull of the old world.

resurrection.name: Resurrection
resurrection.desc: A final, harder test that proves the change is real.

returnWithElixir.name: Return with the Elixir
returnWithElixir.desc: The hero returns home, transformed, bringing something the ordinary world needed.

sevenPoint.name: 7-Point Story Structure
sevenPoint.blurb: Dan Wells's compressed framework. Easy to apply, especially good for short novels and series planning.

hook.name: Hook
hook.desc: The protagonist's starting state — the inverse of their ending state.

plotTurn1.name: Plot Turn 1
plotTurn1.desc: The event that calls the protagonist out of the ordinary world.

pinch1.name: Pinch 1
pinch1.desc: First major pressure from the antagonistic force. Often raises stakes.

midpoint.name: Midpoint
midpoint.desc: The protagonist shifts from reactive to active.

pinch2.name: Pinch 2
pinch2.desc: Second major pressure. The plan falls apart; the mentor often dies here.

plotTurn2.name: Plot Turn 2
plotTurn2.desc: The protagonist gets what they need to resolve the story.

resolution.name: Resolution
resolution.desc: The protagonist executes; the story's questions are answered.

editorSettings.title: Settings
editorSettings.keepStrikethrough: Keep original as strikethrough when accepting an AI change

notes.importTooltip: Import one or more .docx, .txt, .md, .odt, or .epub files as notes
notes.emptyBody: Scratch-pad jottings — pin them to chapters or scenes and they surface in the editor's Notes panel for that spot.
notes.anchorTooltip: Pin this note to a chapter or scene — it appears in that chapter's Notes panel
notes.intro: A {noteTerm} is anything that doesn't fit one of the structured surfaces — research clippings, half-formed scene ideas, cut prose, beta feedback, a thought you want to come back to. Tag it to find it later; pin it to a chapter or scene above so it surfaces there too.

characterAudit.title: Consistency audit
characterAudit.blurb: For each main character, JustWrite sends their profile (role, one-liner, voice, arc, motivation, backstory, established voice samples) plus the prose of every scene that features them. The model flags {flagged} that look inconsistent with the established psychology — not earned by what you've set up about them. Concerns are evidence-cited; small, borderline drifts get a softer flag than out-of-character breaks.
characterAudit.noMainMessage: Mark a character as 'main' in their detail page, then re-open this modal.
characterAudit.idleBlurb: Read every scene this character appears in and audit for consistency against their profile. Change the provider in the chip above first if you want.
characterAudit.noConcerns: No consistency issues across the {scenes} this character appears in.

err.noProvider: Configure an AI provider in Settings → AI to run the audit.
err.noMain: No main characters to audit. Mark a character as 'main' in their detail page first.

sessionRecap.title: Wrap up your day
sessionRecap.idleBlurb: Summarise today's writing and surface open threads worth pinning. Change the provider in the chip above first if you want.
sessionRecap.pinAllTooltip: Drop Loose-thread markers on all unmarked snippets
sessionRecap.threadsBlurb: Snippets the AI flagged as setup-without-payoff in today's writing. Pin one to drop a {looseThread} marker into the chapter so tomorrow's resume briefing surfaces it.
sessionRecap.pinTooltip: Drop a Loose-thread marker on this phrase in the chapter
sessionRecap.pinDisabledTooltip: Snippet not found in current prose — cannot pin

err.nothingToday: No writing recorded today yet — open a chapter and write a bit first.
err.noProvider: Configure an AI provider in Settings → AI to generate the recap.

locations.emptyBody: Places where your scenes happen — linkable from chapters and tracked across the Plot Board.
locations.intro: A {locationTerm} is a place that appears in your story — a city, a tavern, a starship interior, an abandoned house. Use an entry when the place shows up in more than one scene and you want a single source of truth for its layout, history, and sensory detail. Locations feed the {relations} graph and AI features that draw on story-world context.
locations.noScenes: No scenes set in this location yet. Open a scene → Links → Locations to add one.

objects.emptyBody: Items and artifacts that move through the story. Link them to scenes to track their journey across the Relations graph.
objects.intro: An {objectTerm} is a significant prop — a weapon, a letter, a relic, a vehicle. File one when the thing carries weight in the plot or recurs across scenes; throwaway items don't need an entry. Objects feed the {relations} graph and AI features that draw on story-world context.
objects.noScenes: No scenes feature this object yet. Open a scene → Links → Objects to add one.

strands.emptyBody: Narrative strands are the storylines you're weaving. Tag scenes with a strand and it surfaces on the Plot Board as a coloured lane.
strands.intro: A {strandTerm} is a thread that runs through your manuscript — the main plot, a subplot, a character arc, a thematic spine. Write your synopsis and notes below; add {beats} to mark where the thread turns; tag scenes with this strand via each scene's {links} panel. Strand membership also feeds the {relations} graph.
strands.blurbPlaceholder: What is this narrative strand about? (One or two sentences)
strands.bodyPlaceholder: Write the narrative strand in detail — synopsis, character arcs, beats in prose, anything you want to remember…
strands.notFoundBody: This narrative strand no longer exists.
strands.noBeats: No beats yet. Add Inciting / Midpoint / Climax-style turning points so you can see where this narrative strand pays off.
strands.askAbout: Tell me about the narrative strand "{name}"
strands.searchEmpty: No narrative strands match your search.
strands.noScenes: No scenes linked to this narrative strand yet. Open a scene → Links → Narrative strands to add one.

sceneLinks.title: Links
sceneLinks.povQuestion: From which point of view is the scene narrated?
sceneLinks.charactersQuestion: Which characters appear in this scene?
sceneLinks.whenQuestion: When does this scene take place?
sceneLinks.strandsQuestion: To which narrative strand does this scene belong?
sceneLinks.excludeQuestion: Should this scene be hidden from AI retrieval?
sceneLinks.excludeHelp: Keeps this scene out of Ask-the-Book retrieval and any future feature that feeds scene text into an LLM. Useful for spoilers, twists you haven't planted yet, or drafts you don't want surfaced.

critique.structureTooltip: Score tension, hook, pacing, and ending — one LLM call
critique.structureDesc: Scores the chapter as a whole — tension (rising stakes), hook strength (opening pull), pacing (rushed vs. measured), and how the ending lands (cliffhanger, resolved, transition).
critique.structureEmpty: Run a structural pass to see tension, hook, pacing, and ending classification.
critique.notesTooltip: Generate line-level editorial notes — one LLM call
critique.notesDesc: Line-level editor notes across categories like pacing, voice, dialogue, POV, and clarity — grouped into {flags} (clear problems), {suggestions} (concrete revisions), and {observations} (worth noting, no action).
critique.notesEmpty: Run notes to get a list of flags, suggestions, and observations.

err.parse: Couldn't parse notes from the model's reply. Try re-running, or switch the critique model in Settings.

relations.intro: {relations} is a diagnostic graph of how every character, location, and object in your project connects. Edges come from shared scenes, shared groups, and shared strands — you don't draw them here, they appear automatically from the work you do elsewhere. {hover} to light up its connections. Use it to ask whether your protagonist is really at the centre of the story, or whether a major character is isolated.
relations.emptyBody: Add characters, locations, or objects — the Relations graph draws edges automatically from shared scenes, groups, and narrative strands.
relations.hintPin: Click to pin · click again to open
relations.hintPinned: Click node again to open · click empty space to clear

indexBuild.desc: Splits your manuscript into {scenes} and sends each one to the configured {embeddingModel} to build a vector index. Once built, the index powers semantic search and the {chat} panel so you can ask questions about your book and get answers grounded in specific scenes.
indexBuild.staleCleared: · {n} stale chunk cleared | · {n} stale chunks cleared

err.noProvider: No embedding provider configured. Set one in AI Settings.
err.noModel: Provider "{name}" has no embedding model set. Set one in AI → Default embedding (or on the provider).
err.modelChanged: The index was built with "{built}" but the embedding provider is now set to "{now}". Hit Rebuild to re-embed everything against the new model, or switch the embedding provider back to keep the existing index.

batchFill.title: Draft many characters
batchFill.desc: Runs the same two passes as a single character's Fill from book — profile, then voice — for every character you tick, one at a time. Characters with no linked scenes can't be drafted from.
batchFill.autoApply: Apply automatically — empty fields only (skip review)
batchFill.autoApplyHint: Nothing you've written is ever overwritten. Proposals land as each character finishes; review mode is the default.
batchFill.runningAuto: Drafting and filling empty fields as each character finishes.
batchFill.runningReview: Drafting — you'll review everything before anything saves.

err.noScenes: No linked scenes to draft from.

markers.title: Markers
markers.sub: Pins dropped in the prose during drafting — fix-later notes, fact-checks, loose threads, weak passages. Click any tick or row to jump to that spot in the manuscript.
markers.findDanglingTooltip: Scan the whole manuscript for setups that may not have paid off
markers.findAiTellsTooltip: Deterministic scan for phrases that smell of AI — stock verbs, body-language clichés, hedges. No LLM call.
markers.intro: {markers} is the manuscript-wide view of every pin you've dropped while drafting — {fixLater}, {verify}, {weakProse}, {looseThread}, {todo}, {idea}. The timeline strip at the top shows where they cluster across the book; click any tick or row to jump to the marker in the editor. The {findDangling} button asks the AI to scan for setups that may never pay off.
markers.emptyBody: Markers are in-prose pins for fix-laters, loose threads, and weak passages — they gather here so you can triage them at revision time. Drop one from the editor toolbar (pin icon) or with {shortcut} while writing.

export.intro: {export} produces a finished file — {pdf} (typeset with cover and TOC), {docx} (Word with a live TOC), {epub} (e-book for Apple Books / Kobo / Kindle), or a {zip} — the whole book, text and images alike — to keep, move between computers, or open in another app. Pick a format card to see its options.
export.pdfDesc: Print-ready PDF — A4 with serif typesetting, a generated table of contents, and a chapter per page.
export.docxDesc: Editable Word document — keeps chapter headings, scene breaks, and block quotes. Word will offer to refresh the TOC on first open.
export.epubDesc: EPUB 3 — one HTML file per part and chapter, with a navigation document so readers like Apple Books, Kobo, and Calibre show the contents.
export.continuousProseHint: Strip scene titles and {breakMark} scene breaks so each chapter flows as one body of text, like a print novel without ornaments.
export.zipDesc: Everything in this book as one .zip — every part, chapter and scene, the whole story bible, and your images. This is the file to keep as a copy, move to another computer, or open in JustVoice to make an audiobook. Import it back from Settings → Backups.
export.zipJvNote: This is the file JustVoice imports — open it there to cast voices and record the audiobook. It is also how you move the book to another computer.

err.noChapters: Project has no chapters to export.

formatSub.zip: The whole book, to move or share.

versionHistory.listHint: Snapshots of this chapter's scenes, kept on this device. Newest first.
versionHistory.compareTooltip: See what's changed since this version
versionHistory.emptyMessage: Save one before a big revision so you can roll back.
versionHistory.pickHint: Pick two versions to compare. A is the older / baseline, B is the newer.

multiReader.blurb: Four distinct readers each read this chapter through a different lens — a {genre} encountering it cold, a {critic} reading for prose craft, an {intern} deciding whether to flag it for their boss, and a {bookClub} deciding what to discuss. Where the standard Critique modal gives one editorial pass, the panel gives four perspectives — see where the chapter works for each kind of reader and where it doesn't.
multiReader.loadingPrefix: Reading with four lenses in parallel —
multiReader.idleBlurb: Send this chapter to four reader lenses in parallel — a {genre}, a {critic}, an {intern}, and a {bookClub}. Change the provider in the chip above first if you want.

err.noProvider: Configure an AI provider in Settings → AI to run the multi-reader panel.
err.noProse: This chapter has no prose to read yet.

genre.label: Genre-savvy reader
genre.blurb: A reader who's read deeply in this genre and is encountering your book cold.

literary.label: Literary critic
literary.blurb: A close reader concerned with prose craft, voice, image, and what the chapter is doing on the line level.

agent.label: Agent's intern
agent.blurb: A junior agent reading the chapter as a query sample — looking for marketability and hooks.

bookClub.label: Book club reader
bookClub.blurb: A reader who'll bring this book to a six-person book club next month and is reading for what they'll say.

entitySweep.title: Scanning for new entities
entitySweep.desc: Reads the ticked chapters and asks the model for any {entities} not already in your story bible. Same-name proposals from multiple chapters are merged into one, with the originating chapters listed. Nothing is added yet — you review and tick what to keep on the next screen.
entitySweep.matterHint: Front & back matter (glossary, acknowledgments, previews…) is unticked for you — tick anything you do want scanned.
entitySweep.resumeFound: Saved scan found — {done} done{failedPart}. Only the ticked chapters will be scanned.
entitySweep.startOverBody: Discard the saved scan results ({n} chapter of findings)? The next sweep starts from scratch. | Discard the saved scan results ({n} chapters of findings)? The next sweep starts from scratch.

chat.updateTooltip: Embed any scenes added or edited since last build
chat.bibleOnly: Answering from your {storyBible} only — build the index so chat can search and quote your scenes.
chat.buildIndexTooltip: Embed your scenes so answers can quote the manuscript
chat.noSavedChats: No saved chats yet. Ask a question to start one — every conversation lands here.
chat.askAnything: Ask anything about your book — characters, scenes, threads. Follow-ups remember the conversation.
chat.orphanedCharacter: This character was deleted — start a new chat.
chat.askPlaceholder: Ask anything about your book — characters, scenes, threads…

homeShelf.heading: The shelf, oldest at left, working at right.
homeShelf.sub: Scroll right to walk into the unwritten chapters; left to revisit the finished ones.
homeShelf.noChaptersHint: Click "Quick write" above to start chapter one.
homeShelf.noPatterns: start writing to see your patterns
homeShelf.openMarkerPins: open marker pins across the manuscript

foreshadowing.reviewDesc: Setups your manuscript plants that may not have paid off. {dangling} means the setup's key term never appears in a later chapter; {mentionedLater} means a later chapter at least references it — payoff or not is your call. Pin any to drop a {looseThread} marker at the exact phrase so it joins your markers list.
foreshadowing.emptyMessage: No setups without payoff turned up in this scan. Run it again after more drafting.
foreshadowing.pinAllTooltip: Drop Loose-thread markers on every dangling proposal at once
foreshadowing.pinTooltip: Drop a Loose-thread marker on this phrase
foreshadowing.pinDisabledTooltip: Snippet not found in current prose
foreshadowing.runTitle: Reading every chapter for unresolved setups
foreshadowing.runDesc: Reads every chapter and asks the model for narrative {setups} — promises, objects, questions, abilities, secrets, threats, debts — that look like they need a later payoff. After the scan, JustWrite checks whether each setup's key term reappears in any later chapter; the ones that don't are flagged as {dangling}. You review and pin what you want as Loose-thread markers.
foreshadowing.idleBlurb: Scan every chapter for setups that may not have paid off. Change the provider in the chip above first if you want.

err.noProvider: Configure an AI provider in Settings → AI to run the scan.

foreshadowing.pinnedToast: Pinned {n} loose thread. | Pinned {n} loose threads.

plotHoles.title: Continuity audit
plotHoles.blurb: One pass over the whole-book digest plus a tail of each chapter's prose looks for {contradictions}, and {knowledgeErrors}. The model is told to be selective — a clean audit is meaningful, padded findings are noise. Dismissed findings stay on the project but drop out of the default view.
plotHoles.worldRulesHelp: Free-text {rules} — magic-system constraints ("blood magic costs a year of life per use"), hard SF physics ("FTL drives need 48 hours to recharge"), technology limits, social structures. note.delveInto: Stock verb. "Explore" / "investigate" / "unpack" all read more human.

note.aTestamentTo: Greeting-card phrase. Replace with the specific thing that demonstrates it.
note.standAsATestament: As above, in the marble-statue register.
note.embarkOn: Travel-brochure verb. Often just "start" or "set out".
note.inAWorldWhere: Movie-trailer voice. Almost never the right register for prose.
note.shedLightOn: Press-release verb. Show what was illuminated, not that something was "shed".
note.paintAOf: Tell, not show. Show the picture itself.
note.kaleidoscopeOf: Stock metaphor for variety. Almost always cuttable.
note.symphonyOf: Stock metaphor for combined elements. Be specific.
note.myriadOf: Even strict usage prefers "myriad" without "of"; AI uses it as flavour text.
note.herEyes: Cliché. Bodies don't sparkle. Find the actual visible thing.
note.smile: Stock smile-as-emotion-indicator. Replace with the cause, not the smile.
note.heart: Stock fear/excitement tell. Almost always tellier than what could replace it.
note.couldnTHelpBut: Hedged emotional reveal. The character either did or didn't; commit.
note.02: Hedge + filter word; both layers distance the reader.
note.tell: Hedge introducing a half-claim. Pick a side.
note.not130But130: "Not only X, but Y" — over-balanced AI cadence.
note.tellX: Editorial register, almost always tellier than what it replaces.

ai.triggerTooltip: AI writing assist — Rewrite, Expand, Tighten, Continue, Line edits
ai.unstuckNeedsProse: Write a few lines first — Unstuck needs prose to brainstorm from.
ai.highlightSubjectFirst: Highlight a subject first (a place, object, or moment).
ai.rewriteDesc: Rewrite the passage to be more vivid and specific while preserving meaning, tense, and voice. Selection-only because a whole-scene rewrite is too transformative for one click.
ai.expandDesc: Add sensory detail, interiority, and small actions. Roughly doubles the length without changing voice or tense.
ai.describeDesc: Treat the highlighted text as a subject — a place, person, object, or moment — and add 1–2 paragraphs of fresh sensory prose ABOUT it right after. Additive, not a rewrite; the original passage stays untouched.
ai.sensoryDesc: Sibling to Describe. Instead of streamed prose, get a structured pack of short sensory phrases (smell, sound, touch, temperature, taste, movement, social, period detail). Pick the ones that fit and click to drop them into your manuscript.
ai.tightenDesc: Remove filler words, hedges, and redundant phrases. Keeps the meaning, voice, and tense intact — the result is noticeably shorter. Runs on the selection, or the whole scene if nothing is selected.
ai.continueDesc: Write 2–4 more paragraphs from where the cursor is, matching the voice, tense, and POV of what came before.
ai.guidedDesc: Same as Continue, but you give it a one-line instruction first ("Elena confronts Marcus but he deflects with charm"). The next 2–4 paragraphs honour your direction while matching the voice, tense, and POV of what came before.
ai.unstuckDesc: When you're not sure what should happen next, ask the model for five distinct moves (goal shift, interrupt, setting change, reveal, time cut). Pick one and JustWrite drafts the next 2–4 paragraphs in that direction.
ai.lineEditsHint: Selection, or whole scene if none
ai.clearStrikesDesc: Remove every struck-through original left behind by accepted AI changes (and the originals of still-pending ones — that accepts them). The new text stays.
ai.guidedRewriteDesc: Same as Rewrite, but you say how first ("make her colder"). Keeps meaning, voice and tense unless your direction changes them.
ai.dialogueDesc: Writes an exchange at the cursor between the scene's characters, in their story-bible voices. You say what it's about first.

identity.hint: The engine — fill this before anything else.

arc.title: Arc
arc.hint: Frame it as evidence for and against the lie.

voice.title: Voice & presence
voice.hint: How they sound and move — the calibration set.

function.title: Function in the story
function.hint: What they're FOR in the cast.

capabilities.title: Capabilities & limits

classOrigin.label: Class origin → now
classOrigin.hint: Where they started vs. where they are — the gap is characterization. e.g. dockworker's kid → guild master.

education.label: Education
education.hint: Formal or otherwise — it sets vocabulary and what they notice. e.g. street-taught; convent schooling; self-read.

want.label: Wants
want.hint: e.g. win the guild seat; get her sister out of debt

need.label: Needs
need.hint: e.g. to forgive himself; to stop performing for everyone

lie.label: Lie they believe
lie.hint: e.g. “love has to be earned”; “fear gets you killed”

truth.label: Truth they meet
truth.hint: e.g. “they stayed anyway”; “needing people isn't weakness”

fear.label: Core fear
fear.hint: What they organize their life to avoid — the lie's shadow. e.g. being exposed as a fraud; being left again.

lieOrigin.label: Where the lie began
lieOrigin.hint: Write it as a scene: where, who said what, what they decided. e.g. the night her father called her gift a curse.

contradiction.label: Central contradiction
contradiction.hint: Two things both true about them that don't fit. e.g. brutally honest with strangers, lies to those she loves.

values.label: Values under pressure
values.hint: Three values, ranked — the higher wins until the crisis tests it. e.g. loyalty > truth > safety.

heuristic.label: Decision heuristic
heuristic.hint: One line: “under pressure, they choose ___ over ___.” e.g. protects the crew over the mission.

stakes.label: Stakes
stakes.hint: What breaks — for them and others — if they fail. e.g. the harbor floods; his daughter loses her name.

start.label: Beginning
start.hint: e.g. hiding the gift, keeping her head down

midpoint.label: Midpoint
midpoint.hint: e.g. forced to use it in the open

end.label: End
end.hint: e.g. leads openly — or doubles down and loses them

accent.label: Accent
accent.hint: e.g. soft Southern drawl; clipped city vowels; none

vocabulary.label: Vocabulary
vocabulary.hint: words they favor. e.g. nautical slang; courtroom Latin

tic.label: Speech tic
tic.hint: a verbal habit. e.g. starts sentences with “Look,”

sample.label: Sample line — calm
sample.hint: an ordinary line, in their voice. e.g. “Chart it or lose it.”

register.label: Register
register.hint: Formal ↔ casual — where they sit, and when they slip. e.g. courtly in public, gutter-blunt alone.

rhythm.label: Rhythm
rhythm.hint: Clipped or flowing; do they interrupt or trail off? e.g. short sentences, always interrupting.

forbidden.label: Forbidden words
forbidden.hint: Words this character would never say. e.g. never “sorry”, never “please”.

subtext.label: Subtext habit
subtext.hint: How they avoid saying the real thing. e.g. answers a hard question with a joke.

humor.label: Humor style
humor.hint: Dry / absent / cruel / self-deprecating — “none” is a choice too. e.g. deadpan, never laughs at his own.

languages.label: Languages
languages.hint: What they speak or read — who can they understand that others can't? e.g. reads Old Parian; speaks the trade cant.

sampleAngry.label: Sample line — angry
sampleAngry.hint: An actual furious line they'd say. e.g. “You had one job. One.”

sampleLying.label: Sample line — lying
sampleLying.hint: A line they say while covering or deflecting. e.g. “I was never near the place.”

physicality.label: How they occupy space
physicality.hint: Posture, gait, stillness or motion — one line a scene can borrow. e.g. still and watchful; takes up no space.

presentation.label: Presentation
presentation.hint: What their appearance choices signal — the message, not the looks. e.g. an expensive coat kept deliberately shabby.

stressTells.label: Baseline & stress tells
stressTells.hint: Their normal state, and how fear or lying leaks through. e.g. over-precise hands; goes very quiet.

theme.label: Thematic argument
theme.hint: The side of the story's central question they embody. e.g. lives out “mercy is weakness” — and is proven wrong.

protagonistRelation.label: Relation to protagonist
protagonistRelation.hint: Opposition / mirror / temptation / ally / measuring stick. e.g. mirror — same wound, opposite choice.

selfImage.label: Self-image
selfImage.hint: Who they believe they are. e.g. “a realist” (really a coward).

persona.label: Public persona
persona.hint: Who they perform being. e.g. the unflappable captain.

privateTruth.label: Private truth
privateTruth.hint: Who they actually are — the gaps between these three are engines. e.g. terrified he's becoming his father.

buttons.label: Buttons
buttons.hint: What reliably provokes them — levers other characters can pull. e.g. mention his brother; call her naive.

allegiances.label: Allegiances & obligations
allegiances.hint: Groups they belong to — and what membership demands. e.g. sworn to the Order; owes a smuggler a life.

escalation.label: How they escalate
escalation.hint: Aggression, withdrawal, sabotage, going over heads… e.g. goes cold and starts quietly planning.

cornered.label: Cornered behavior
cornered.hint: What they do with no good options — who they really are. e.g. burns it down rather than kneel.

abilities.label: Abilities
abilities.hint: Magic, tech, training — what can they actually do? e.g. reads emotions; deadly with a thrown knife.

costs.label: Costs
costs.hint: What each use takes — energy, sanity, time, moral weight. e.g. every casting costs a day of her life.

limits.label: Hard limits
limits.hint: What they can never do — limits make more plot than powers. e.g. can't lie while touching cold iron.

conditions.label: Conditions
conditions.hint: What the ability requires — tools, materials, states. e.g. needs moonlight; needs the true name.

whoKnows.label: Who knows
whoKnows.hint: Who is aware of these capabilities. e.g. only her old mentor knows.

physicalConstants.label: Physical constants
physicalConstants.hint: Only features that appear on the page. e.g. burn scar on the left hand; limps in the cold.

health.label: Conditions & disabilities
health.hint: Anything that changes what's possible in a scene. e.g. deaf in one ear; needs the tonic daily.

timelineAnchors.label: Timeline anchors
timelineAnchors.hint: Birth year + dated events — do the math once. e.g. born 1147; the fire was year 12.

knows.label: Knows at story start
knows.hint: What they already know as the story opens. e.g. knows the king is dead; knows who the traitor is.

doesntKnow.label: Doesn't know
doesntKnow.hint: What they don't know yet — and might act against. e.g. doesn't know she's being followed.

believesWrongly.label: Believes wrongly
believesWrongly.hint: The top source of continuity errors and POV leaks. e.g. believes her brother is still alive.

secrets.label: Secrets
secrets.hint: One per line: the secret — who else knows — the reveal. e.g. “killed the steward — only Mira suspects”.

possessions.label: Possessions with story weight
possessions.hint: Objects that will matter — and where each one is. e.g. the dead brother's watch (in her coat).

regrets.label: Regrets
regrets.hint: Compressed backstory plus motivation in one line. e.g. the letter he never sent.

family.label: Family / upbringing
family.hint: Who raised them and what it cost. e.g. estranged from a father who runs the guild.

skills.label: Skills & ceiling
skills.hint: Competence AND its ceiling, so solutions stay fair. e.g. brilliant tactician, hopeless liar.

routines.label: Routines & habits
routines.hint: Useful mainly for disruption when broken. e.g. tea at dawn, always the same cracked cup.

appearance.label: Appearance beyond the constants
appearance.hint: The changeable look, beyond the fixed constants. e.g. tall, ink-stained fingers, never quite still.

tastes.label: Tastes & quirks
tastes.hint: Small preferences that make them a person. e.g. hates music; collects old maps.
